acceptance_checks: Re-acquiring a lock for a task in status review leaves it in review; a task in planned still becomes ready.
Re-acquiring for a task in running or repair-needed preserves that status.
A task whose contract locks are a strict superset of its granted locks is reported as a grant/contract divergence naming both sets, not as a bare 'locks are not granted'.
Refreshing a grant that would collide with another task's active lock fails and names the owner.
Amending a task's locks does not require a manual lock re-acquisition before dispatch.
non_goals: Changing what locks mean at MergeGate
Auto-widening a grant into another task's held locks

findings.detail: git diff main...HEAD includes ~200 .shiki records (goals/tasks/ledger/runner/reports/worktrees/plans/repairs) and unrelated mergegate/workflow/docs changes from already-merged goals, because the task branch was cut from a stale local main. MergeGate derives its base from origin/main where these already exist, so they resolve to an empty real PR diff. The actual task change is scripts/shiki_tasks.py, tests/test_lock_lifecycle.py, and the lock-lifecycle block in scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh. Non-blocking; consistent with prior clean reviews in this goal lineage.
findings.title: Diff carries large stale-local-base mirror/workflow state

findings.detail: cmd_dispatch_check → evaluate_lock_grant → refresh_lock_grant rewrites the lock record and appends a lock ledger when a contract-widening amendment left the grant behind. This is the acceptance-required behavior ('amending locks does not require manual re-acquisition before dispatch') and is idempotent: once the grant covers the contract, the issubset early-return prevents further writes. refresh_lock_grant preserves task status verbatim, so the loop's planned-only _unblock is unaffected. The added refreshed_at key is benign (locks are outside the schema-conformance loop).
findings.title: dispatch check now mutates state on a diverged grant (intended self-heal)

scope:
Two defects on the same seam in scripts/shiki_tasks.py, both observed live on PR #179. (a) cmd_lock_acquire and try_acquire_locks set task['status'] = 'ready' unconditionally (lines 373 and 691), so re-acquiring a grant rewinds a task that already has an open PR from review back to ready — MergeGate's post-CCA rule then blocks it. Preserve any status at or beyond 'running'; only planned may become ready. (b) A Spec Amendment that widens a task's locks silently invalidates its own grant, because the grant is checked as a superset of the contract; nothing in the amendment path refreshes it. Detect the divergence and either refresh the grant or fail with a reason naming it, rather than surfacing as an unexplained 'locks are not granted'.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes. On 2026-07-27/29 a single task was driven from Goal to PR twice (#179, merged; #181, open at the time of writing). The loop's judgments were autonomous; the plumbing between them was not. Seven manual interventions were required, and this task removes one of them.
  Manual step removed: re-acquiring a lock by hand after every contract amendment.
  Observed: three amendments (A3, A3b and the earlier A-LOCKS widening) each invalidated their own grant, surfacing only as 'locks are not granted' with no indication that an amendment caused it; one re-acquisition also rewound a task with an open PR from review to ready and blocked MergeGate.
  Reproducible when: amending a contract's locks leaves a valid grant, or fails with a reason naming the divergence, and no re-acquisition ever moves a task backwards through its lifecycle.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Make lock acquisition preserve task lifecycle and follow contract amendments
